- REF-003: implemented by Claude Code on the user's sequential request; root delegated these shared integration changes. (1) `postal-mime@4.1.4` pinned exact (zero runtime dependencies, explicit nesting/header/part/forward limits). Mailparser's own documentation marks it maintenance-only and recommends PostalMime; the only published PostalMime advisory (GHSA-f2hq-32vh-53cc) is fixed from 4.0.8. Declared charsets the runtime cannot decode are refused rather than read as windows-1252; `.html`/`.txt` must be UTF-8, BOM-marked or (HTML) `<meta charset>`-declared. (2) Durable pre-upload admission: `admit_email_file_upload` binds actor + tenant + request key + SHA-256 + kind + size + name and reserves capacity under the tenant lock (20/hour, 200 active, 500 added emails, 100 MiB stored-or-reserved distinct bytes) before any service-role write; `finalize_email_file_upload` enqueues one `email.import` job only after the stored object size is confirmed; replays resume at the interrupted step; nothing deletes objects, so an object used by another receipt is never removed. Storage allows overlapping writers to the same path (last wins) but refuses later ones; the path is the SHA-256 of the server-validated bytes and the worker re-verifies, so racing writers store identical bytes. (3) Trusted worker RPCs `claim_/finish_/fail_email_file_import` are service-role only, re-check active tenant and active uploader, and accept parsed output only for the frozen hash and still-stored object. Legacy `claim_job` (selection and stale sweep) and `private.onboarding_lease` (so `fail_job` and fixture finishers) now refuse `email.import` as well as `email.rewrite`; `job_runs_kind_check` gains `email.import`. (4) Trusted format: `reference_imports` gains `source_kind`, `file_import_id`, `content_format`; `create_email_result` is redefined in 90015 to use `content_format` when present (pastes keep the 90014 regex inference), and choose/preview/copy text version/rewrite worker read the same stored format (`sourceFormat`, `email_sources.format`). `pastedReadable` takes an optional trusted format. (5) New private bucket `email-imports` (5 MiB, html/plain/rfc822), no client write policy, owner/admin read policy for referenced objects. `GET /api/v1/email-imports/:id/file` and export `part=file` serve exact bytes; `part=original` keeps its meaning (decoded source). `next.config.ts` applies the sandbox CSP override to both download paths. (6) Server-only pilot gate `EMAIL_IMPORT_TENANT_IDS` (exact UUIDs, max 50, no wildcard) for any non-loopback or production Storage; checked before admission, before the write, on retry and on each worker attempt; independent of the unchanged OpenAI pilot gate. Root must add the blank name to `.env.example` (this session cannot read it). (7) `SubmitButton` gains optional `pendingLabel`/`disabled`; the setup reference step adds a secondary "Upload a file" link beside "Paste an email". (8) Review fixes: metadata/name/download shortening is surrogate-safe (`clipText`, `wellFormed`); HTML decoding follows BOM → explicit `<meta charset>` → UTF-8 and refuses undecodable declarations; dates outside years 1–9999 are dropped as metadata. (9) Narrow shared UI integration requested by root now that real rewriting is being configured: `AppShell` takes an optional `status` (default "Your workspace" / "Emails are saved privately"; admin and designer layouts pass their own truthful line) and shows the brand's demo copy only when `AUTH_MODE=demo`; the mobile menu shows the same status; the client overview footer reads "Sending and performance data use samples. Emails you add and create are saved." outside demo mode. `BrandPresentation` is unchanged, and no simulated sending/results behaviour changed. (10) Final deployment-compatibility correction: Vercel Functions cap request and response bodies at 4.5 MB (https://vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations, https://vercel.com/docs/errors/function_payload_too_large), so the raw upload/storage bound is 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) everywhere — browser hint and help text, action, parser, SQL `byte_size` and admission checks, bucket `file_size_limit` — keeping uploads plus multipart overhead and original-file downloads under the cap. Earlier REF-003 evidence used 5 MiB; it was superseded by this change and re-verified. The 100 MiB workspace cap, admission, pilot gate, 100,000-character decoded bound and the existing `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` (used by other upload features) are unchanged; files above 4 MiB need direct-to-Storage signed uploads, recorded as remaining. (11) Root supervisor integration, not overwritten by this task: blank `EMAIL_IMPORT_TENANT_IDS=` in `.env.example`; CI browser job runs `node scripts/test-email-import-concurrency.mjs` with a 25-minute browser timeout; the deployment snapshot was moved outside the repository. A narrow, supervisor-authorized test fix in `tests/e2e/email-generation.spec.ts` makes the preview-fit helper wait (retried poll, no sleep) until the published `data-scale` matches the measured container before the unchanged fit assertions.

- REF-002: implemented by Claude Code on the user's sequential request. Twelve calendar months (UTC) of purchaser protection wins over the 180-day order candidate rule; consent, bounce/spam, existing suppression and changed evidence are rechecked at each stage. Two original local winback audits precede ten-day nonresponse suppression. Concurrent active sweeps are rejected. Reversal removes only the optimizer reason when all consent/protected-reason checks pass. Dated fictional band pricing is an estimate with no measured savings. Own/reference reuse copies structural metadata into an unapproved original draft; cross-client publication remains off.

Learning uses complete seven-day same-cohort sends within thirty days, five per subject-length side; only owner-pinned preferences influence matching fixture copy and retain evidence lineage. Re-synthesis never changes dismissal. Ten consecutive first-time confirmed synthetic sends is the default L2 streak; any owner rejection resets its generation. L2 simulation is actor/policy/brand/version-bound at 72 hours; production L2 and design delegation remain constrained off.

- V2-008: GROS visibility is checked by RLS and every mutation; a shared conversation never transfers proposal authority. Package cycles retain immutable definitions, atomic synthetic usage is reserved before generation, and actual fixture usage is reconciled by operation. Verified-email invitation acceptance is derived from local Auth. Operator diagnostics contain metadata/counts only. The shared worker helper now treats a missing JWT role as denied, avoiding nullable-boolean authorization.

- V2-007: immutable provider schedule precision is milliseconds, matching the package ISO snapshot. L1 is an explicit revisioned owner policy; it does not grant general chat authority. Every provider mutation requires server-recorded conclusive reconciliation, not just a worker convention. Rescheduling retains provider identity while adding a new immutable package; rejected cancellation retains actual remote state. Only an explicit labelled simulated send creates a private own skeleton. Sent snapshots remain immutable during later asset/kit corrections. The live Klaviyo class remains disabled: public campaign/send-job contracts were checked, but hosted artifact, account acceptance and transport reconciliation are unverified.

- V2-006: deterministic fixture design artifacts use trusted, self-contained SVG strips in a private server-write-only bucket; text-email HTML remains readable without slicing. This needs no rendering dependency. SVG email-provider/client compatibility and aesthetic quality are externally unverified; live delivery stays disabled. Package assembly is rebuilt from approved sources, never caller HTML. Per-strip revisions retain unchanged content-addressed artifacts, and own templates remain tenant private and originate only from confirmed simulated sends.

| Decision            | Value                                                                                          | Reason                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runtime             | Next.js App Router + TypeScript                                                                | One deployable web application with server-rendered role surfaces.                                         |
| Architecture        | Modular monolith with explicit domain modules                                                  | Fast MVP iteration without premature distributed-system overhead.                                          |
| Hosting             | Vercel                                                                                         | Preview deployments and server functions.                                                                  |
| Backend             | Supabase Postgres/Auth/Storage/Realtime/Queues                                                 | Durable relational core and tenant security.                                                               |
| Isolation           | Server authorization plus PostgreSQL RLS                                                       | Deny-by-default tenant boundaries with defense in depth.                                                   |
| Data access         | `@supabase/ssr` plus generated database types and SQL/RPC                                      | Keeps RLS authoritative and avoids a competing schema source.                                              |
| Validation          | Zod                                                                                            | Shared environment, form, action, and adapter validation.                                                  |
| UI                  | Tailwind CSS + accessible headless primitives                                                  | Fast, consistent, responsive implementation.                                                               |
| Tests               | Vitest + Playwright + pgTAP/SQL security tests                                                 | Covers code, user journeys, and RLS.                                                                       |
| Async               | Durable queue + idempotent workers                                                             | External API work must survive retries and timeouts.                                                       |
| Demo behavior       | Seeded fixtures + fake adapters                                                                | Complete workflow without external secrets or billable calls.                                              |
| Dates               | Store UTC; render in tenant IANA timezone                                                      | Removes the timezone contradiction found in the reference product.                                         |
| Money               | Integer micro-USD internally                                                                   | Avoids floating-point cost errors.                                                                         |
| IDs                 | UUID primary keys; external IDs in unique scoped columns                                       | Stable internal identity and provider reconciliation.                                                      |
| Visual system       | Cool neutral field, white panels, graphite actions, blue interaction cues                      | Matches the user-selected reference theme through original semantic tokens.                                |
| Design review       | Brand owner reviews/revises and approves the exact current design version                      | User-confirmed correction; admins handle assignment, SLA, and escalation.                                  |
| v2 build scope      | New implementation on existing foundation; email-first fake/fixture execution                  | Autonomous plan in `docs/OVERNIGHT_BUILD_PLAN.md`; external actions remain separately authorization-gated. |
| Approval / delivery | Revision-bound approvals; immutable package; reconcile unknown provider outcomes               | Aligns diagrams and target contracts; V2-000 owns code/type/migration integration.                         |
| Autopilot default   | L0 owner confirms; L1 standing policy after owner approvals; production L2/delegation disabled | Preserves owner design control while permitting simulated background scheduling.                           |

Confirmed: reference-neutral visual direction, white-label-first architecture, code-first build path, DRY shared implementation. The selected Impeccable direction uses seed `6f728f1c`; its durable contract is `DESIGN.md` plus `.impeccable/design.json`.

Connections shows the Klaviyo card only; the Shopify card, form and `connectShopify` action are gone (the credential helpers, verifier, `shopify-read` port, `store-data` reader, `features/store` dashboard and the tables stay, unused, with no destructive migration). `/store` redirects to `/brand` and the Brand & Store tab row is not shown (one tab left). The Dashboard's UTM tile no longer asks to connect Shopify. Empty product lists say products will come from the Klaviyo catalog (the live catalog is V2-S3a, #310). The Sample data tools keep the product fixture, which still uses the internal `shopify` connection row for its `commerce.sync` job, but call it "sample catalog" on screen. The brand-mismatch guard keeps its Shopify checks; they never fire without a Shopify connection.

- RET-002 (2026-11-11): decisions D16 and D17. - STR-001 (2026-11-11): the Brand pulse (`features/strategy/pulse.ts`). Code builds the evidence (each fact with an id and its words) and decides what may be offered: only real codes, valid on the window's first day, at or under the max discount (others are listed as left out with the reason). The agent (`brand-pulse`, purpose `review` = Flash, as AGENT_MAP's model table says; the Brief writer and Calendar planner will use `plan`) only picks evidence ids and says why, without numbers, codes or dates; `checkPulseAnswer` enforces that and out-of-stock products. Up to 3 tries with the exact problems; a refused call (cap, provider) is not retried; then `codePulse` and one fallback entry. The owner's pick is `OfferPick` (`auto`, `none`, `picked` offer ids from the pulse only); STR-003 stores it with the plan run. Sample store in `features/strategy/sample.ts` until lane B's readers land. After review: `readPulseInput` checks the store data (a bad brand or start throws; a bad row is left out and counted); `until` is the code's real last day, inclusive in store time (copy QA's `expiresAt` must be the end of that day); out-of-stock products are never launch or bestseller facts; `statedFact` (`features/strategy/words.ts`) refuses digits, money signs, number words, promise words ("free shipping"), weekdays, months and the store's codes as whole words; `tryAgent` (`features/strategy/retry.ts`) is the one retry loop for every agent.

- STR-002 (2026-11-11): the Competitor mapper (`features/strategy/competitors.ts`). Code keeps library emails of the same industry and size band from the last 90 days, places each on our 15 days (the same number of days, 0–7, before a date of the same kind: holiday, sale or event; or 0–6 days before month end when our month end is in the window), and groups them into patterns counted by distinct brands (at least 2). The agent (`competitor-mapper`, purpose `review`) sees only pattern ids, timing, types, offers, angles and counts (no email ids, brand ids, names or words), picks patterns and names each move without numbers or quotes; code writes "2 days before Public holiday: 3 of 5 similar brands. …" and the confidence (brand share). Same 3-try check and fallback as the pulse. `LibraryEmail` is the shape CI-001's Email classifier should feed. After review: its `industry`, `brandSize`, `emailType`, `offerType` and `angle` come from lane B's closed lists in `features/intelligence/taxonomy.ts` (CI-001, imported, not copied), so no competitor name, subject or phrase can ride in a label; untagged emails (null labels) are left out; rows that do not match (or have a broken date) are left out, and `readMapperInput` refuses a broken start.

- STR-003 part 1 (2026-11-11): `planFifteenDays` (`features/strategy/plan.ts`). Brief writer (`brief-writer`, `plan`) writes up to 8 actions (goal, fact ids from the pulse and the competitor moves, a date range in the 15 days, an allowed offer or none); Calendar planner (`calendar-planner`, `plan`) turns them into up to 10 slots (action, date, local time, one of 8 email types, angle, up to 3 products, offer, audience); the calendar rules (`calendarProblems`, code) refuse days outside the window or the action, no-email days, unknown or out-of-stock products, offers not allowed or already ended, unknown audiences, numbers in angles, more than the owner's sends per week, two emails to one audience on a day, and, with the shared planning policy, offers above 40% of a week's emails and offers closer than 7 days; the Strategy critic (`strategy-critic`, `review`) adds its own problems. Up to 2 rounds give the planner both lists; whatever still fails is dropped and logged. Agents that cannot answer fall back to `codeBrief` / `codeSlots` (logged); a critic that cannot answer leaves the rules alone (logged). Facts, prices and codes in the plan come from code, never from an agent. After review: `readPlanInput` refuses a pulse for other days, bad dates or send times, and keeps only the pulse's own offers; the kept plan is re-checked after every drop (`keepPassing`), so dropping an email can never leave a week above the offer share; the planner gets its previous plan with slot indexes and every problem when revising, the round with the fewest failing slots is kept, and a planner refused while revising keeps its best plan; the critic has the usual 3 tries; rules have stable keys (`CalendarRule`), new ones tie offers to offer emails, keep send times in 07:00–21:00 and refuse products before their launch day; `existing` covers the 7 days before the window too; drops are logged under `calendar-rules` (with the rule keys) or `strategy-critic`; the planner sees at most 30 products; with 2 emails a week no offer fits, and the plan says so in `notes`.

The `section-planner` agent (purpose `copy`, Flash) picks variants by id; `checkSections` requires real variants of allowed families, the logo header first (after an optional announcement bar), the footer last, one button, one hero, products within the slot's count and an offer banner only with an offer. Then the usual 3 tries and a logged fallback to a safe layout per email type (`codeSectionPlan`), which always passes the check. `maxOutputTokens` is the answer's room only: MEM-002 (#370) adds the Gemini 2.5 thinking budget in the provider.
- EML-002 (2026-11-11): layer 2 of the email build (`features/email-build/content.ts`). Code locks each value from its source: products from the catalog (`productLock`: in the catalog, featurable, https photo, fits a product section, a known price; a repeated id counts once, the first), the slot's offer from the discount codes (`offerLock`: on the list, within the max, still working at send time; the percent and end come from the code, the end shown in store time), pictures from the catalog or the confirmed photos, links by `storeLink`'s rule. What cannot be locked becomes a safer choice: another product, no offer (also when no offer section is left, so the writer never gets a code it cannot show), a smaller product section (`product_grid_3col` → `product_grid_2col` → `product_feature`), a product hero for a picture hero without a photo, or no section; replaced sections use the family's seed variant and the email always keeps a message. At most 6 products are locked (`maxLocked`, the job boundary's `focusProductIds` limit). The `content-locker` agent (purpose `copy`, Flash, no thinking) only places product ids into the product sections, and only when there is a choice; `checkPlacement` enforces exact counts, known ids, each once, the plan's main product first and planned products before others; 3 tries, then plan order (logged). Changes are logged once per email as `content_replaced` with fixed words (`changeWords`, `didWords`) and the change keys. Contracts: `LockedContent.input` is the narrowed `AssemblyInput` (only the locked products in section order as `focusProductIds`, only the locked code as `offerCode`); `assembleLocked` (`features/assembly/modes.ts`) is the Copywriter on exactly the locked sections, so each locked product lands in its locked section (tested from the lock to the written email). Shared changes in ASM-001/003: `productTakes` is the one product-placement rule (`fill` and the sample writer): a grid shows 4 or 6 only when the later product sections still get their fewest (`minProducts`, also used by the Section planner); `layoutSequence` budgets the fewest products per section; `storeLink` uses a store link only when it is a real link, the first product's page only when there is none, and no link sections when it is broken.
- EML-003 (2026-11-11): the end of layer 2 (`features/email-build/inspect.ts`). `writeAndInspect` runs the Copywriter on the locked sections (`assembleLocked`), then code checks first, every round: assembly's own problems, copy QA (`checkCopy`, ASM-002) on the locked facts and code, a lock check (the draft shows exactly the locked products and code), `priceChecks` (a money amount the writer writes must be exactly a locked product's price) and `emailChecks` (subject at most 60 characters, at most one exclamation mark and no capitals words, preview 20 to 140 characters and not the subject, `spamPhrases`, no web or email address typed into the words, one button section, every link one the Content locker locked, alt text on every picture, at most 300 words). The checks read only the writer's words: `protectedText` masks product names, the brand name, the code, its percent and end, reviews, the founder's note and photo descriptions, so the writer is never asked to change what it cannot. Code is the final word: only a draft that passes code goes to the `brand-inspector` (purpose `review`, reads the Brand book and do's and don'ts) and the `email-inspector` (purpose `label`); each returns problems with a field, an exact quote of the writer's own words (`checkInspection` refuses store words), a reason and a fix; a draft seen before reuses its verdict. Feedback carries the last two rounds' reasons. The first write plus `rewriteRounds` (3) rewrites; then plain copy (`assembleLockedPlain`: facts-only words that never say "new", subject within 60, `Draft.source` `plain`), which must pass the same code checks, else nothing is built. Writer errors: busy or down (`rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `timeout`, `ledger_unavailable`) returns `retry` for the job; no writer (`cap_reached`, set-up or account problems, refusals) and the fake writer go to plain copy with their `cause` (`allowance_used`, `no_live_writer`; plain copy from the fake is sample-mode copy and must be treated like ASM-001's sample drafts); a wrong-shape answer is a round with its exact problems; `AssemblyError` and bugs throw. One fallback entry per email (`copy-inspectors`, `copy_plain_fallback` or `copy_failed`) with the cause and only code rule keys as candidate don'ts for LRN-002; an inspector that cannot answer is logged once and skipped. Contracts: `Draft.source` gains `plain` (ASM-001); `writerRules` gains the inbox limits.

- EML-004 part 2 (2026-11-11): "Create email" end to end (D17). Migration `email_builds` (number at merge, D24): one build per planned email at a time (`build_queued` → `push_queued` → `drafted`, or `failed`) and one `push_key` per planned email: a new build after a failed one that reached the push keeps its key, so "Try again" never makes a second Klaviyo draft (blueprint: unknown remote outcomes reconcile before a repeat). The owner's `create_email_build(t, run, slot)` (owner only, tenant locked first, the latest plan only, the run planned, the email's day not passed in the workspace's timezone; clicking again returns the open or drafted build); service-role `claim_email_build` (pushes first, 5-minute lease; brings the planned email, the push key, the workspace timezone and the plan's first day; a failed step waits a minute; 3 attempts), `finish_email_build`, `finish_email_push`, `fail_email_step(code, final, retry_after_seconds)` (a busy Klaviyo's wait is kept in `not_before` and does not use up an attempt, at most 20 waits). `buildEmail` is the code-only path for now, like STR-003 part 2: the safe section layout, products placed in plan order by the Content locker (`agent: false`), plain facts-only copy that must pass every code check, coded design A; no AI call. It builds in the workspace's one brand timezone (`tenants.timezone`), reads offers through DSC-001's `OfferSource` at the send time (`offersAt`: no answer or no max means no discount), and the sample store starts from the plan's first day. Offers (supervisor, 11 Nov): `ownerOrSampleOffers` reads `SupabaseOfferSource.managed` with the job's service-role client; a saved max (a `brand_offers` row) or any active code wins, even while the store is the sample store; only when the owner saved nothing do the sample offers from the plan's first day apply; a failed read gives no discount, never the sample. Limits: after 5 failed builds a planned email is not built again (PT409); a step whose planned day has passed (store time) fails as `day_passed` when claimed; the push step gets its own attempts and waits; a built email needs a subject. A product is unfeaturable only when its stock is known to be 0 (`featurableStock`): unknown stock is allowed. `runEmailBuilds` checks the built email's shape and size before storing it, fails refused finishes at once, and pushes through `DraftPusher` with the push key; the owner's click runs both steps right after the reply, the cron sweep runs up to 10 waiting steps in 5 s. `DraftPusher` (`lib/providers/klaviyo-draft.ts`, contract agreed with the supervisor): draft only, never schedule or send; one idempotency key per planned email, and the same key updates that draft to the email just built (a draft the owner already scheduled or sent is refused as `rejected`, never changed); never throws, failures as `auth`, `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`, `unavailable`, `rejected` with the failing launch checks; it uploads the pictures and runs the launch check before creating the draft; a `sample` email is refused by a live adapter; PSH-001 builds it, `fakeDraftPusher` until then. `StoreSource` (`features/email-build/ports.ts`) is sample until lane B's readers. The plan shows each email's state ("Creating…", "Putting it into Klaviyo…", "Sample draft (not in Klaviyo)" or "In Klaviyo as a draft", or the failure's reason with "Try again"); no button for a day that has passed. `/plan/email/[buildId]` shows the built email through the safe preview (`previewHtml`, `ScaledFrame`) with plain notes.
- EML-005 part 1 (2026-11-11): the A-vs-B test harness (`features/email-build/ab-test.ts`, D21). Up to 10 planned emails for one brand are each built once (`lockedDraft`, split out of `buildEmail`: the same sections, locked content and plain copy) and drawn twice, so only the drawing differs: A with coded blocks and B with one designed hero picture, each with one Visual inspector look on the same terms (not the production retries, so neither side gets a best-of-3); an email without a product hero is not drawn with B (no picture paid for); an inspector that gives up is not asked again for the rest of the run, and no B picture is paid for after that (`not_judged`); B is `made`, `no_hero`, `not_judged` or `picture_failed` (logged once per email); only a sendable B (`bSendable`: made, inspected, and nothing wrong in its picture's section or the whole email, VISION rules 9 and 10) is ever a variation B, while an unsendable B's looks still count in the comparison. `summarize` is paired: each score is averaged over the emails where both sides have it, with the counts shown. Scores per drawing: looks (the Visual inspector's new 1 to 10 `score`, prompt version `2026-11-11.3`; null when not inspected, e.g. no AI; an older answer without a score still passes), deliverability by code (`deliverability`: 100 minus 40 at or within 10 KB of Gmail's clipping limit, 50 for no words, 20 for fewer than 40 words per picture, 10 per spam phrase as whole words up to 30, 20 for a designed picture over 1 MB when the picture maker reports its size; words counted without the hidden preheader or Klaviyo tags), and clicks per delivered email once results exist. **Sending (supervisor, 11 Nov, option a):** each planned email goes into Klaviyo as one draft with A and B as two variations of the same content, day and audience, split 50/50 with no automatic winner, and the owner still schedules it (D17); PSH-001 creates the variations and LRN-001 reads results per variation. Fall back to alternating A and B across planned emails only if Klaviyo's API cannot create a campaign with two variations at a 100% test size, and record that here. The owner's 1 to 5 stars are optional (D16: no run waits on the owner); `summarize` works without them and leaves out anything missing or out of range. Part 2: the comparison page and the owner's saved default (`email_design_default`, A until he picks), which "Create email" then draws with; the test runs as a leased job with a spending cap (it is long, paid work, and a re-run makes new pictures).
- EML-AB (2026-11-16): **A versus B in "Create email"** (D21; AGENT_MAP §4 "How an email gets drawn": B is the default to test). When the design studio's email passes every check (the hard checks and the whole-email check), the design step stores it as design B (`approach` B; before, it said A) and the same email drawn with its coded blocks (the same content and words, through the same hard checks) as `designA`. The worker pushes the two as variations of one Klaviyo draft (PSH-001's even test: half the audience each, no winner picked; the owner still schedules it, D17). Only the coded design is stored beside the email, never design B twice: each design is under Gmail's size (DST-005), so both fit the 290 kB stored. Logged in fixed words (agent `ab-test`): design A failed a hard check (B goes alone as a draft, `ab_no_coded`), or the draft could not hold both designs (PSH-001 answers design A only when Klaviyo refuses the even test, when the planned email's draft was first made with one design, or when it takes over an existing message: `ab_one_design`, once per planned email). Every designed email is tested this way until the owner picks the default (EML-005 part 2's `email_design_default`); nothing changes while `DESIGN_STUDIO` is off.

- STR-003 follow-up (2026-11-11): "Plan next 15 days" reads offers by the email build's rule (`ownerOrSampleOffers` on DSC-001's `SupabaseOfferSource`, supervisor 11 Nov), in the workspace's one timezone (`tenants.timezone`): the owner's saved max and codes win even on the sample store; the sample offers only when nothing is saved; a failed read retries the step (`offers_unreadable`) within its normal 3 attempts, never the sample; on the last attempt the step goes on with no offers (0%, no codes), says so on the screen and records one `plan-offers` / `offers_unreadable` entry in the fallback log, so a plan is never stuck (supervisor, 11 Nov). **`until` changed:** an offer's `until` is now the last store-local day an email can send with it (`lastSendDay`): the day it ends when it still works after the latest send time (21:00; Settings ends a code at 23:59:59, so that day stays), otherwise the day before. The pulse lists the codes working when the first day begins and leaves out, with the reason, those ending before an email could use them. The plan step keeps only picked offers that still work (current percent and `until`, their facts rewritten), one note names any left out, and every offer email is checked at its own send time the way the email build checks it (`plan_offer_unusable` guard). The stored pulse holds up to 200 offers and left-out codes (DSC-001's limit).
- REL-081 (2026-11-14): "Create email" runs as saved steps (owner pick 81). Migration `email_build_steps` (number at merge, D24) adds `email_builds.step` (`sections` → `content` → `copy` → `design` → `push`; `push` exactly when the email is stored) and `progress` (each finished step's output by name, at most 300,000 bytes). Jobs save a step with `finish_email_step(build, lease, done, output)` (PT409 for a step out of order, 22023 for a non-object or too large output); `finish_email_build` now needs the `design` step; `claim_email_build` returns `step` and `progress` and hands out the furthest step first. Table displays and `list-style: none` are allowed. The section format (DST-001a) now refuses what the reader refuses, in its styles and in each inline style, and reads every link (in attributes too) with it, so a `url(` inside a string can no longer hide one; the page it draws turns list markers off, so an `<ol>` draws no numbers. - PIC-26 part 1b (2026-11-16): **the subject line lab** (owner pick #26 "Subject line lab"; `features/email-build/subject-lab.ts`, on part 1a's evidence). Up to 10 subject ideas for one email (`labSize`) are weighed against how the store's own past emails were opened, and the best two are kept: A goes out, B is the one worth testing against it. An idea's score is the sum of its traits' lifts (`learnFrom`, part 1a); a trait the store's emails do not show counts only by a small rule of thumb (short +0.5 points, long -1, an exclamation mark -0.5), which a trait they show never gets. Ties keep the writer's order (its own pick first). The open rate it points to (`expected`) is the store's mean moved by each trait with evidence, by how much more or less the idea has it than the store's emails do (a trait half of them have moves it half its lift either way). Ideas the same but for case and spacing count once (the same subject again is tried while none of its spellings fitted, since another preview line may), at most 10 are tried; an empty one or one over 120 characters is left out; the caller's checks (`fits(subject, index)`: the copy checks, a subject another email of the plan has, the preview line written with it) leave out an idea before it is weighed, and each idea keeps its place in the list given (`index`, to find its preview line again). B is the best idea after A that differs from it in a trait (`tests` names them: what the test teaches), has less than 60% of the two ideas' words in common, and scores at most 5 points below A (`testMargin`, `worthTesting`: half the audience gets it); none: no test. `subjectLabVersion` is kept with what it picks. Each idea comes with up to three reasons in the owner's words, the strongest first ("Subjects that ask a question: 31% opened, the others 26% (6 of 12 emails)."; none when the two rates round the same) and, with evidence, the open rate the store's emails point to. Plain code, no AI and no database: the same ideas and history give the same pick.
- PIC-26 part 1a (2026-11-16): **what a subject does, and what the store's past emails say about it** (owner pick #26 "Subject line lab"; `features/email-build/subject-traits.ts`). Each subject has traits found by plain code (`traitsOf`): short (30 characters or fewer, a first-name tag read as a name, a logic tag and unseen characters left out), long (more than 50; a phone shows about 35), a question, a number (only in a subject without an offer), an offer (`offerWords`, ONB-103's), an emoji (a flag and a keycap too; never ©, ® or ™), the reader's first name (Klaviyo's tag, in its three spellings), the store's name (as a whole word, or its tag), a deadline as a phrase ("ends tonight", "ends in 3 hours", "24 hours only", "today only", "last chance"; never "the story never ends"), an exclamation mark, all lower case (never a script without capitals), something new (new, just in, back in stock, restocking; never "New Year", "New York" or "just in time") and "you" ("yourself" too); a tab or a line break is a space. The past emails that can teach (`pastSubjects`) are the history's sent emails with a subject of at most 300 characters, an open rate above 0 (none opened is opens not tracked) and at least 100 recipients, never an A/B test (its rate mixes two subjects) or one still collecting its results. With 10 of them or more (`minPastEmails`), each trait shown by at least 3 emails, and missed by at least 3 (`minPerSide`), gets the difference between the mean open rate with it and without it, shrunk by how sure it is (d² / (d² + se²), se the difference's noise from each group's own spread of open rates, never below the store's spread and at least 1 point, and how many emails each side has: one lucky email among three is noise, not a trait) and kept within 15 points (`learnFrom`); its two open rates and counts are kept for the reasons the lab gives in the owner's words (`traitWords`). Fewer emails, or a trait too few show, say nothing. Plain code, no AI and no database: the same history gives the same evidence.

A letter (`letterSchema`) is a subject, a preview line, an optional greeting, one to eight paragraphs, a sign-off, the name that signs (and who they are), an optional P.S., and the store's links, which code gives it (the locked content), never the writer. (the greeting, sign-off and name are drawn as plain words) and never on words a reader cannot see. (was ...)", "... removed (was ...)"). `parseRevenueGoal(text, { currency, today })` is strict: the whole text must be an optional lead ("goal:", "I want", "target"), at most one period ("this month", "next month", a month name with or without a year) and one amount (whole digits or commas, at most two decimals, an optional k or m, a listed code before or after, or a symbol before), so "$20k this month", "Goal: 20,000 AUD next month", "€5,000 for December", "1.5m in March 2027" are read and "20% off", "20-30k", "20.000", "I may want 20k", "20k last month", "about 20k", "cancel the 20k goal" are null. Root cause of every scheduled failure since 6 Nov: the secret went into `curl --config -` as `header = "Authorization: Bearer …"`; a line break in the stored secret made curl refuse the config (`option --config: is unknown`, HTTP 000), so no call reached the app. The owner turned off GitHub failure emails: the lane checks the Actions tab after a batch of merges.

The book is built in full, his corrections are applied, and only then is it cut to its 7,000 characters: the readers' observed lines go first, then their audience names, his own lines last (matched per section). A workspace keeps at most 200 live corrections (`correct_brand_book`, `PT409`, migration `20260914090073`), so `listCorrections` (at most 500) never stops a book from being written. `staleBooks` also counts the owner's newest correction made or taken back since `since` (up to 1,000 rows of each, the 100 newest changed workspaces looked up): a book older than it is written again by the next readers' run. The review page (#58) should also write the book right after a correction (`writeBrandBook` in `after()`), so agents see it at once.
- ONB-065a (2026-11-15): **suggested competitors are inbox brands of the same industry** (owner pick #65, data only until the page spec is approved). `suggestCompetitors` (`features/onboarding/suggested-competitors.ts`) gives up to 10 brands the Inspiration inbox is subscribed to, each with a plain reason ("Also a pet brand, and sent 6 emails in the last 30 days.", "Also an apparel brand."). The store's industry is `correctedIndustry` (what it sells as the owner corrected it, as "Create email" reads it; a real store ignores sample findings); a brand's is the label most of all its emails carry (at least 2, more than half, `other` never wins), else its niche's words (`industryInWords`, whole words, as the store's own words are read). **The database picks the brands** (`suggestable_inbox_brands(t, since)`, migration `20260914090075`): members of the workspace only; subscribed brands of the workspace's own kind (from `brand_profiles.synthetic`; no profile: none); never a brand the workspace follows or once followed; each with its emails since `since` and its label counts (never an email itself, the counts from their own index); at most 500, busiest first. **This widens what a workspace reads:** until now only the brands it follows; now also the names, sites and niches of these. **For now only the sample store gets suggestions:** a real store gets none, because anyone who signs up and saves a real brand profile would then see up to 500 of the inbox's real brands (name, site, niche, how often they send); that waits for Raman, with following real brands. The store's own website is left out (`www.`, a link or a subdomain is the same website). "Other" gets nothing. Order: emails in the last 30 days, then the newest email, then the domain. `readCompetitorSuggestions` reads with the person's own client (row rules for the workspace's rows). Not yet: "similar size" (VISION; the store's own size is not known yet). **Needs Raman:** whether real stores may see the inbox's real brands (one line in `suggestable_inbox_brands`), following a real brand (`subscribe_competitor` takes `.example` domains only) and signing the inbox up to brands it does not get yet.
- ONB-060b (2026-11-15): **the Site reader keeps the brand's two logos and "Create email" uses them** (owner pick #60, part b). A live read of the brand's website finds the logo candidates on its home page (`logoCandidates`, with the brand's name and the page's final address after redirects), reads each one an email could show (`keepableLogo`: https on the standard port, no name or password, a format Klaviyo imports, so never SVG or WebP, at most 1,000 characters) through `SiteFetcher.picture` (https on 443 from any public host, since a store's pictures are often on its platform's; PNG, JPEG or GIF only; at most 1 MB; 3 seconds each, none started without that time left; never a private address), and picks one for light sections and one for dark sections (`findLogos`, `pickLogos`) **only from pictures really read as PNG, JPEG or GIF by their own bytes** (`emailPicture`), while the other pages are read. When no picture could be read, nothing earlier is replaced. It keeps them before its findings (`record_site_logos(job, lease, on_light, on_dark)`, under the job's lease; the newest read wins), in `brand_logos` (one row per workspace: the site, the two https pictures of at most 1,000 characters, never the same picture for both; members read it; only the worker writes). A logo that cannot be kept is logged and the read goes on, and a failed logo read never fails "Create email" (the emails show the brand's name). Only a live read keeps logos: the sample site keeps none, so sample emails show the name, never a picture that cannot load. The email build's store gives `logo` (dark ink, for the light header) and `logoOnDark` (new `BlockBrand` field) to the blocks, only when the logos were read from the workspace's current website (`www.` aside).
- ONB-057c (2026-11-15): **one industry rule for the plan and the email** (follow-up to ONB-057b and ONB-058). `industryFrom(findings, { live, corrections })` (`features/onboarding/strategy-data.ts`) reads the industry from what the brand sells as the owner corrected it: his own added lines first, then the readers' surest, with his removals and replacements (`applyCorrections`, case and spacing aside); `words` is the line it comes from, which the key dates match. `onboardedStrategyData` reads his corrections (`listCorrections`, with the offering findings and the brand name) and passes them to the key dates and the plan; a failed corrections read throws (the step is tried again). `correctedIndustry` ("Create email", ONB-057b) is now this same rule. The two can still see different findings (the planner drops the sample rules' only for a live history, the email store whenever any finding is real; the planner reads up to 500 offering findings, the email store the 500 newest of every topic), so they may still differ in rare cases.
- ONB-059a (2026-11-15): **the photo library's site part finds a page's photos and tags each one** (owner pick #59, part a; pure). `sitePhotos(html, page, kind, { brand })` (`features/onboarding/site/photos.ts`) returns up to 30 photos per page, surest first: a product's pictures in the page's structured data (`Product`, `ProductGroup`, `ProductModel`, `IndividualProduct`, by name or IRI; addresses, `ImageObject`s and `@id` references), then its share picture (`og:image`, `twitter:image`), then the pictures in the page: one per `<picture>` (its JPEG or PNG sources first), each at its largest size (`srcset` before `src`), lazy pictures by their real address (`data-src`, `data-lazy-src`, `data-original`, `data-srcset`; never a stand-in or a `{width}` template). Each is tagged **product** (on a product page, in a product card, or linking to one of the brand's own product pages) or **lifestyle** (the brand's world elsewhere), with its description (at most 200 characters, never half of one) and its page. **Only photos an email can show** (`emailPhotoUrl`): a `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png` address on a public host (never an IP, a one-word host, one ending in a dot, `localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.test`, `.example`, `.invalid` or `.onion`, nor Instagram's or Facebook's picture servers, whose addresses expire), https on the standard port, no name or password, no other format asked for (`format`, `fm`, `fmt` or `output` in the query, Cloudinary `f_webp`, Cloudflare `/format=webp,…/`), at most 1,000 characters. **Never the brand's logo:** the pictures of any link to the home page (the header's, a top bar's), `og:logo`, `itemprop="logo"` and every `logo` in the structured data are noted while the page is read, and no photo may be one of them (at any size, in any format: an SVG logo rules out its PNG copy); nor a picture named or described as a logo, or a file naming only the brand (its wordmark; a product's own structured-data pictures aside). **Never:** icons, badges, seals, flags, swatches, ratings, payment marks or stand-ins (brand words aside: "Icon Apparel" is a name), one stated smaller than 200 px (or 0), hidden ones (`hidden`, `display: none`; `aria-hidden` only hides from screen readers, so it counts), video, audio and SVG, boxes of other brands' marks or customers' photos (press, "as featured in", logo lists, partners, payment, seals and certifications, social and Instagram feeds, reviews and review widgets), or any picture of the page's header, menu or footer, by tag, by role (`banner`, `navigation`, `contentinfo`) or by words (`site-header`, a `…__footer` section); their structured data is still read. "As featured in" and "as seen on" count only as side-by-side words, never an animation class (`slide-in`). A store's own "featured" sections count. The same photo at several sizes (`?width=`, `_400x`, `@2x`, `_crop_center`, `.progressive`) is kept once, at its largest, with any copy's description and product tag. Page pictures (500) and structured-data and share pictures (500) are capped apart, so the surest are never crowded out. The site's own name (`cedarlane` in `shop.cedarlane.com`) counts as a brand word. The page is parsed once and walked without recursion; attributes are cut before they are read, so a hostile page cannot crash it. The logo finder's address, `srcset`, word and landmark helpers are shared (`absolute`, `largestOfSet`, `words`, `landmarks`, exported from `logos.ts`).
- ONB-059b (2026-11-15): **the photo library keeps the site's photos and joins the catalog's** (owner pick #59, part b). A live read of the brand's website reads each page it fetched for its photos (`sitePhotos`; never without the time a model call may take, so never at the findings' expense; a page over 1 MB is not read for photos, since the parser cannot be stopped once started; a page that fails is logged and skipped), joins them in reading order, each once (`photoKey`), at most 200 (`maxSitePhotos`), and keeps them before its findings (`record_site_photos(job, lease, photos)`, under the job's lease): the workspace's set is replaced whole (even with none), unless a newer read already kept its own (then false, nothing changes; `brand_photo_sets` names the read that kept the set and the plain website it read, so a newer empty set still wins); a set with one bad photo is refused whole and the earlier set stays; when no page could be read for photos, nothing is replaced. `brand_photos`: one row per photo (address, product or lifestyle, page, description, where on the page, position), members read, only the worker writes. Photos that cannot be kept are logged and the read goes on. `readPhotoLibrary` (`features/onboarding/photo-library.ts`; the member's own client, or the worker's after a membership check) gives the library: the catalog's own product pictures first, each with its product, never one of a product no email shows (unpublished, a duplicate, another currency) (only the sample products while the catalog was read from the fake Klaviyo, never mixed with a real store's; none while it was never read), then the photos of the kept set (read by its own read), only while they come from the workspace's current website (the owner may have changed it); only photos an email can show; the same photo from both once, as the catalog's, with the page's description when it has none.
- REL-ONB2 part a (2026-11-16): **"Create email" gets the store's own reviews, from its own Reviews reader only** (follow-up to DST-007 part 2b). `storeMaterial` (`features/onboarding/store-material.ts`, pure) gives `Store.confirmed` (new optional field, `AssemblyInput['confirmed']`'s shape) from the findings the readers kept, and `assemblyFor` carries it, so `allowedBlockTypes` allows the review strip exactly when there are reviews and code places them word for word (the Copywriter never writes one). The reviews are the `quotable_review` findings (ONB-105, chosen by code): only from the workspace's current website or one of its subdomains (`onDomain`; never its parent or a sibling), at least as sure as a fact (0.6), never a sample-rules finding in a live workspace; with their own stars (a review without stars is left out, never given some); their exact words of at most 200 characters (`maxQuote`; a longer one is left out, never cut); the reviewer as first name and last initial (`reviewerName`: "Jordan Smith" is "Jordan S.", "Dr. Jane Smith" is "Jane S.", a one-word name as it is; a placeholder, a place or a pair ("from Leeds", "Kate and Sam"), a suffix ("Jr.", "III") or more than letters leaves the review out, never an initial made up); best rated and newest first, at most 3, each once. **Only while the brand has a verified review source** (`facts.reviewsVerified`, ASM-001's and copy QA's rule, kept: the strip shows each review's stars and copy QA refuses stars without one). A quote is left out when it names someone (the reviewer, another customer, the staff: customer words' `namesSomeone` on each sentence, the brand's and its products' names aside, and the reviewer's own name words), has spam words (`spamPhrases`), a claim, a result or an effect on the body (customer words' checks, now exported), or fails copy QA with the store's facts judged **with no product title and no brand name masked** (the Brand inspector masks only the products an email places, so the pre-check is at least as strict). **No customer photos** (`ugc_grid`): no reader keeps customers' own photos (the Site reader leaves review photos out) and a brand photo is never one. **No founder note yet** (`founder_note`): the Site reader matches a quote case aside and keeps the model's letters, so nothing proves an about-page quote is a whole sentence of the page; marking that on the finding needs a migration (the evidence's keys and an offering's value are checked by `record_site_findings`). Text emails are unchanged (no confirmed founder, so letters are still signed by the store's team). The sample store (`sampleStoreFrom`) keeps none.

## Migration allocation

To reduce parallel conflicts, each workstream owns a numeric migration block. Do not renumber an already shared migration.

| Range            | Owner                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `2026091400xxxx` | Foundation/extensions/helpers        |
| `2026091401xxxx` | Identity/tenancy/RLS                 |
| `2026091402xxxx` | Brand/AI/prompts/usage               |
| `2026091403xxxx` | Integrations/jobs/Klaviyo/Shopify    |
| `2026091404xxxx` | Campaigns/calendar/audiences         |
| `2026091405xxxx` | References/competitors/templates     |
| `2026091406xxxx` | Designers/submissions                |
| `2026091407xxxx` | Support/feedback/notifications       |
| `2026091408xxxx` | Packages/reporting/admin additions   |
| `2026091409xxxx` | Integration fixes/materialized views |

New migrations after the hosted project reached `20260914090016` use the next `2026091409xxxx` number, whatever their domain. Since 2026-11-06 the Supabase GitHub integration applies every migration merged to `main` to the live database, and the hosted project refuses out-of-order versions. **Since 2026-11-11 (D24) there are no reservations:** right before merging, rename an unmerged migration to the next number after the newest on `main`, then re-run `test:db`. On `main`: `090017` (UIR-013 connection profiles), `090018`–`090019` (UIR-005 brand profile sections and facts), `090020`–`090021` (UIR-011 Settings), `090022`–`090023` (UIR-012 Holidays), `090024`–`090025` (UIR-019 Team), `090026`–`090027` (UIR-020 Feature Requests), `090028`–`090030` (UIR-023 brand timezone), `090031`–`090032` (UIR-021 brand-mismatch guard), `090033`–`090034` (UIR-009 Inspiration), `090038`–`090039` (INB-001 inbox), `090040` (INB-002 images and screenshots), `090043` (INB-003 sections and facts), `090044`–`090045` (INB-004 ops queue and brand directory), `090046` (GEM-002 live AI usage), `090047` (GEM-003 platform AI budget), `090048` (MEM-001 agent memory), `090049` (KLV-001 live Klaviyo), `090050` (CI-001 competitor tags), `090051` (RET-002 agent fallbacks), `090052` (CI-002 block variants), `090054` (DSC-001 max discount and discount codes), `090055` (ONB-101 brand findings), `090056` (STR-003 part 2 strategy runs), `090057` (ONB-102 catalog reading), `090058` (EML-004 part 2 email builds), `090059` (ONB-103 Klaviyo history; numbered at merge time). `090035`–`090036` (UIR-008 Ask GROS, parked) are older than `main` and must be renumbered before they merge.

Use a valid 14-digit Supabase migration version inside the assigned UTC-hour namespace, for example `20260914010000_create_tenants.sql`, then increment seconds monotonically. The namespace is an ordering device, not a claim about wall-clock creation time.

No numbers are reserved (D24): GEM-002 and GEM-003 merged as `090046` and `090047`; the `090060`/`090061` reservation they once had is void.

## Release checklist

- [ ] Database resets from zero with migrations and safe seed.
- [ ] Generated Supabase types match the final schema.
- [ ] Typecheck, lint, unit, integration, RLS, and Playwright suites pass.
- [ ] Client/admin/designer authorization is deny-by-default.
- [ ] Two-tenant negative-access suite passes.
- [ ] Service-role key never appears in a client bundle.
- [ ] External credentials are encrypted or held only in platform secrets.
- [ ] Queue consumers use leases, attempts, idempotency keys, and dead-letter behavior.
- [ ] Cron endpoints validate a secret and do not trust public callers.
- [ ] AI usage checks run before provider dispatch and reconcile actual usage afterward.
- [ ] File buckets and signed URLs enforce tenant/assignment access.
- [ ] Security headers and rate limits are enabled.
- [ ] Production contains no demo passwords or destructive seed behavior.
- [ ] Preview smoke test completes the P0 campaign journey.
- [ ] Rollback and operational runbooks are documented.

### 2026-11-06 — STAB-001 — scheduled job worker

- Status: review
- Branch/worktree: `claude/stab-001-scheduled-job-worker`, branched from `main` at `9e9d56c` and updated with `main` by merge.

- Changed contracts: new `GET /api/internal/jobs` scheduled sweep and `features/cron/scheduler.ts`; `scheduledDispatchAllowed` in `features/cron/gate.ts`. New root `vercel.json` (cron only), `.github/workflows/scheduled-jobs.yml`, and a `scheduled-sweep` project in `playwright.config.ts`. See Global decision STAB-001. Register: EXE-022 (atomic queue claiming) moves to `verified_fixture`.
- Migrations: none.
- Verification run: `pnpm verify` passed (format, lint, typecheck, 311/311 unit tests in 60 files, 21 new: scheduler ordering, empty queue, waiting work outside the active-workspace page, bounded rounds, time budget, no empty round, workspace cap, per-workspace failure isolation, due/stale read failures, excluded paid kinds; route 401 for missing/wrong/non-bearer/unset secret and before any configuration check, 503 for live mode and missing service configuration, safe 500, counts-only body; adapter gate). Fresh local reset → `pnpm test:db` 600/600. Fresh reset → full `pnpm test:e2e` 80/80 in 11.9 minutes on a lean local stack (studio, analytics, vector, imgproxy, edge runtime, realtime, meta and pooler excluded), the two scheduled-sweep journeys last: three simultaneous authorized sweeps finished three queued copy jobs in two workspaces with `attempt = 1` and one generated version each; a paused workspace's job stayed `queued`/`attempt 0`; a repeat sweep changed nothing; a job whose retry wait had passed and a job left `running` with an expired lease both finished on attempt 2; a job whose fourth attempt had an expired lease became `failed` (`stale_lease`) with no fifth try; unauthorized `GET`s returned 401. The workflow's `curl --config -` header passing was checked against a local echo server with a dummy value.
- Review: `code-reviewer` found no security, tenant-isolation, owner-authority or live-provider defects. Its findings were all fixed: the 10-minute schedule used Actions minutes even without a secret (now opt-in through `SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENABLED`); waiting work beyond the first 1,000 active workspaces could be skipped (the active filter is now in the due-job query); retry and stale-lease paths were untested through the sweep (two journeys added); the sweep spec did not really run last (now its own dependent project, full suite re-run); the URL override could send the secret anywhere (removed; HTTPS only); a failed-visit warning was added; round counting and docs were corrected; rotation steps were documented.
- Known issues: GitHub Actions is disabled for the repository, so neither CI nor the 10-minute schedule runs until the owner enables it and sets `SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENABLED`; the daily Vercel cron needs `CRON_SECRET` in Vercel Production. At 10 minutes the schedule uses about 4,400 Actions minutes a month on this private repository (above the free allowance); the runbook lists slower options. AI rewrites and file imports still resume only from the owner's page. No admin last-run status screen yet (OPS-014). Concurrency evidence shows each job ran once while three sweeps were in flight; it does not prove the sweeps' claims interleaved, which the database lock makes serial per workspace anyway.
- Next consumer: owner adds the secrets, enables Actions and the schedule; STAB-002 can then hide the "Run … jobs" buttons from owners.

The password change checks the session first, verifies the current password with `createStatelessClient()` (new `lib/supabase/stateless.ts`: anon key, session in memory only, signed out after use), then calls `auth.updateUser`. Shell: `ShellNavigation` gains optional `profileHref`; only the client navigation sets it (`/profile`), so admins and designers no longer see a link to a page they cannot open. For Gemini 2.5 with a `reasoningEffort`, the provider adds the thinking budget on top (`geminiOutputTokens`: low +1,024, medium +4,096; capped at 65,536), because 2.5 counts thinking as output and a cut-off inside the thinking came back as `incomplete` (no answer, no retry). Digits are not English words, so number-heavy copy ("Save 20% on 3") is less often graded. Each line counts as a sentence, so many short lines (buttons, eyebrows, step titles) lower an email's grade: a hard paragraph among many short lines may pass. A plural title ("Cedar Candles" for "Cedar candle") is not masked. Words per section count the whole section, headings included. A Copywriter that keeps a section too long ends in plain copy after its rewrites, as any other finding.
- Next consumer: the Copywriter's and the Letter writer's rewrites; the results-based learning (LRN-002) that could tune the targets.

### 2026-11-11 — CI-004 — retry the browser job's system packages

- Status: review
- Branch/worktree: `claude/ci-004-browser-retry`
- Commit(s): see the CI-004 pull request.
- Changed contracts: `.github/workflows/browser.yml` and `inbox-screenshots.yml` install Chromium, then its system packages best effort (`apt-get` with 2 retries and a 20 s timeout, then `playwright install-deps chromium`; browser.yml tries twice). The step has `continue-on-error` and a 5 to 6 minute limit, so if apt stays unreachable the job carries on: ubuntu-latest already has every library Chromium needs, apt only adds optional fonts, and a truly missing library still fails the journeys at launch. Twice on 11 Nov (#380, #381) the runner could not resolve the Ubuntu mirror and the browser job failed before any test ran. Proposed by lane A on #381; azure.archive.ubuntu.com was unreachable from the runners for over 2 hours.
- Migrations: none.
- Verification run: `vitest run tests/ci/workflows.test.ts`; the PR's own browser job runs the new steps.
- Known issues: none.
- Next consumer: every PR.
